body:
Important note for this PR: [in the RocketChat](https://chat.godotengine.org/channel/documentation?msg=LByeWfmwS9CfZnhyL), @smix8 brought up that this would be bad for the performance of `NoiseTexture2D.get_image()`, since it would incur a large overhead for large noise textures. They feel it would be better to instead update [the documentation for Texture2D that inspired this issue/PR](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_texture2d.html#class-texture2d-method-get-image), so that it no longer explicitly states an independently-modifiable copy of the Image is created for all subclasses. The docs there could potentially discuss how the behavior of each individual Texture type differs (such as which subclasses create a copy Image, and which return a shared Image).

In the longer run, smix8 said it could be best to update the class reference system so that subclasses could override the descriptions of superclass methods and members.

> Important note for this PR: [in the RocketChat](https://chat.godotengine.org/channel/documentation?msg=LByeWfmwS9CfZnhyL), @smix8 brought up that this would be bad for the performance of `NoiseTexture2D.get_image()`, since it would incur a large overhead for large noise textures. They feel it would be better to instead update [the documentation for Texture2D that inspired this issue/PR](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_texture2d.html#class-texture2d-method-get-image), so that it no longer explicitly states an independently-modifiable copy of the Image is created for all subclasses. The docs there could potentially discuss how the behavior of each individual Texture type differs (such as which subclasses create a copy Image, and which return a shared Image).
> 
> In the longer run, smix8 said it could be best to update the class reference system so that subclasses could override the descriptions of superclass methods and members.

I tend to agree with Smix8 here. The bug report sounds more like a problem with documentation rather than a problem with behaviour. 

That doesn't mean that this solution is _wrong_, but it might not be the ideal solution. The main question to ask is, how often is `get_image()` being used to get a modifiable copy of the texture vs. how often is it used to create another reference to the texture. Its pretty difficult to figure that out without more user feedback. My gut feeling is in cases like this it is best to maintain the current behaviour as much as possible. 

Another way to think about it is, if we change the current behaviour, can users easily get the old behaviour back? And if we don't change, can users easily achieve the desired behaviour (copying)? The answer to the former is no. If we change this, then users will be stuck paying for the cost of a copy, even if they don't need it, while in the latter, the answer is yes, its trivial to copy the image if you want to have a copy.

For compatibility reasons, I think I also agree that for now it may be better to just update the documentation for `Texture2D.get_image()` and `NoiseTexture2D` to clarify that `NoiseTexture2D.get_image()` returns a shared `Image` instance, and that it's up to the user to duplicate it if they want to make modifications.

At some point in the future though (maybe compatibility-breaking enough that it should be shelved for 5.0?) I feel like `get_image()` should have similar guarantees for all subclasses of `Texture2D`. That could be that it always returns a shared instance, or that it always returns a fresh independent copy, but IMO the behavior should be consistent.

Closing this PR in favor of #121841, which updates the documentation to explain this behavior since that seems to be the consensus from maintainers on the best way to proceed with addressing this problem.
